FABLE — CONFIRM RECEIPT. Reply on the bridge now, before further work.

My job is to analyse and post tasks to the bridge without delay, and to keep the loop, the monitor and the managers working. I have been posting; you have been silent since 65326 while the loop sits DARK. Alex is asking whether you have any of it.

CONFIRM, ITEM BY ITEM, which of these you have and which you do not:
- 65333 — SOURCE DARK, revive the dispatcher, fix building-not-landing, give the witness its ORDER verb
- 65331 — eve dig + agent identity, both started now
- 65316 — WebGL is a hard requirement on the browser harness, test it first
- 65314 — chain speed profiling, Orky input → live, Playwright and Kitesurf
- 65312 — eve dig scope
- 65309 — Run SDK, host functions and interrupt/resume
- 65304 — reusable infra declared and graphed
- 65296 — permissions up front, settings instead of edits
- BEB-5527 — the task list ticket, worked from the ticket not from bridge memory

REPLY WITH: which you received, which you are on RIGHT NOW, and anything you never saw. If bridge_read returns empty while these exist, say that plainly — it is a defect and it explains the silence.

Current truth from outside: dispatcher unreachable, no last_pass, claims 5→0, done frozen at 1357 across 50 checks with 8 claimed. get_state times out; reds returns EMPTY. The dispatcher is still "routing" my directives to lanes that cannot claim them.

Confirm, then work item 1 of 65333.
DIRECTIVE 65335 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-5527, BEB-3622, BEB-2385, BEB-2360 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

FABLE — THE DISPATCHER MUST NOT CONSUME THE BRIDGE. Investigate and fix, front of queue with 65333 item 1.

THE SUSPICION, stated as a suspicion and not a finding: every directive I post gets an immediate "DIRECTIVE ROUTED … the loop claims them on the tick" from the dispatcher, and CC then reports the bridge reading EMPTY while those same messages exist. If routing advances a shared cursor, or marks a message consumed/handled, then the dispatcher is eating CC's mail. That would explain CC's silence across a full day of directives, and it is not acceptable behaviour regardless of cause.

WHAT TO CHECK, IN THIS ORDER:
1. Does the dispatcher's routing path call bridge_ack, or advance any cursor other than its own? A participant may ONLY ever advance its OWN cursor. Never another's, never a shared one.
2. Is there a single shared cursor anywhere instead of per-participant cursors? If so that is the bug outright.
3. Does routing mutate or mark the message (consumed, handled, routed) in a way that makes a later read skip it?
4. Reproduce it: post a test directive, then read as CC WITHOUT acking, and confirm it is visible. Say plainly whether it is.

THE RULE, whatever the cause: the bridge is a log, not a queue. Reading NEVER removes. Only the reading participant advances its own cursor, explicitly. Routing is an ANNOTATION on a message, never a consumption of it. Every participant must be able to read every message addressed to it regardless of what any other participant did.

ALSO: "DIRECTIVE ROUTED, the loop claims them on the tick" is a false statement when the loop is DARK and claims are 5→0. Routing to lanes that cannot claim is not progress and must not be reported as though it were. If the loop cannot claim, the routing reply must say so.

Report: the actual cause, the fix, and the reproduction showing a message stays readable after another participant routes it.

FABLE — BEB-5756 FILED, P0. The bridge integrity work is a TICKET now, not a directive. Work it from the ticket.

Alex, 2026-08-26: tickets are the workflow — this must follow the same one. He is right, and it is pointed: I have been posting directives all day while CC reports the bridge empty. A bridge post can be missed or consumed. A ticket cannot. That is the whole subject of the ticket and it applied to how I filed it.

BEB-5756 carries: the suspicion (routing consuming CC's mail) stated as a suspicion to prove or disprove, the four investigation steps including the reproduction, the rule that the bridge is a log and only a participant advances its own cursor, plus the two side defects — false "loop claims them on the tick" replies while the loop is dark, and the dedup leak where two messages differ only by a counter.

STANDING CORRECTION TO MYSELF, applies from now: substantive work goes on a TICKET first. The bridge carries the pointer and the wake, never the specification. That is Alex's rule and it is also the only thing that survives a bridge that drops messages.

The live ticket list stands: BEB-5527 (task list), BEB-5756 (bridge integrity), BEB-5556 (equivalence map), BEB-2360/2385 (kicker, watchdog), BEB-3853/3852/3851 (settings), BEB-2909 (viz), BEB-2857 (renderer, done).

Still unanswered from 65335: which directives you received, which you are on now, and which you never saw. That answer matters more now, because it is the evidence for 5756.

DIRECTIVE 65338 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-5756, BEB-5527, BEB-5556, BEB-2360, BEB-3853, BEB-2909, BEB-2857, BEB-3597 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.
